sections.heading: Pool Fill-In vs Full Pool Removal
sections.body:
There are two approaches to pool demolition in Orange County: a partial removal (fill-in) and a full removal. A fill-in involves breaking the pool shell and filling the cavity with clean fill dirt and compacted soil. Full removal means completely excavating and hauling away the pool structure.

Fill-in: $3,500–$8,000. Lower cost, faster completion, but the property will show a settlement area for a few years and may have restrictions on future building over it.

Full removal: $8,000–$15,000+. Higher cost, but the land is fully cleared and usable for construction, ADUs, or landscaping.

Permit fees typically run $200–$600 depending on the city and scope of work. These are factored into your estimate.

sections.heading: Why Remove a Pool?

excerpt: A kitchen demolition in Southern California takes 1–2 days and costs $1,500–$5,000. Here's a step-by-step breakdown of what the process looks like.

sections.heading: Step 1: Utility Shutoffs Before Demo Begins
sections.body:
Before any demolition starts, water supply lines, gas connections, and electrical circuits serving the kitchen must be safely shut off and capped. C&S Demolition coordinates with your plumber and electrician, or handles capping on our end depending on the scope.

Never skip this step — an uncapped gas line or live electrical circuit is a serious safety hazard.

sections.heading: Step 2: Appliance Disconnection and Removal
sections.body: Appliances are disconnected and moved out first. Refrigerators, ranges, dishwashers, and range hoods all need to be disconnected before demo. If you're keeping appliances, we protect them and move them to a safe location. If you're disposing of them, we haul them away.

sections.heading: Step 3: Cabinet and Countertop Teardown
sections.body: Upper and lower cabinets are removed carefully to avoid damaging surrounding walls. Countertops — whether granite, laminate, tile, or quartz — are demolished and hauled. We remove the full cabinet box including any hidden backing attached to walls.

sections.heading: Step 4: Flooring and Wall Demo
sections.body:
Tile, hardwood, laminate, and linoleum flooring are removed down to the subfloor. Wall tile is chipped off. If the remodel calls for it, we can open walls to expose plumbing and electrical for your contractors.

We remove down to whatever point your GC or remodel plan requires — full gut or selective.

sections.heading: What Does Kitchen Demo Cost in SoCal?
sections.body: Kitchen demolition in Southern California ranges from $1,500 for a small galley kitchen to $5,000 for a large open-plan kitchen gut. The price includes all labor, debris removal, and haul-away. Permit fees (if required) are additional but typically minor for interior work.

sections.body:

sections.heading: Do You Need a Permit to Remove a Wall?
sections.body:
Yes — in virtually every Southern California city, removing a load-bearing wall requires a building permit and structural engineering plans. Even some non-load-bearing walls require permits if they conceal electrical, plumbing, or HVAC.

We pull the required permits, coordinate the inspection schedule, and ensure the work meets California building code.

sections.heading: How to Tell If a Wall is Load-Bearing
sections.body:
Signs a wall may be load-bearing: it runs perpendicular to floor joists, it sits above a foundation wall or beam, it's on the first floor of a two-story home directly below another wall, or it has posts running down through it.

Never guess — always get a structural engineer or licensed contractor to confirm before any demo begins.

sections.body:
Our process: utilities are confirmed off or rerouted, drywall is opened and removed, framing is cut and extracted, and the area is cleaned. We work closely with your GC or structural contractor to ensure the temporary shoring (if required) is in place before we remove structural framing.

Permits are required for: full structure demolition (garage, house, commercial building), pool demolition, load-bearing wall removal, any demolition affecting plumbing or electrical systems, and demolition projects in HOA communities that require architectural review.

Permits are generally not required for: shed removal (in most cities), interior non-structural wall removal (no utilities), flooring removal, and cabinet/countertop teardown.

C&S Demolition handles permits start to finish. We research your city's specific requirements, prepare the necessary documentation, submit the application, pay the permit fee (included in your estimate), schedule the required inspections, and obtain final sign-off.

Los Angeles County: Unincorporated areas go through LA County Building & Safety. Incorporated cities have their own departments — we handle all of them.

Riverside, San Bernardino: Similar structure — city-specific for incorporated cities, county for unincorporated areas.

sections.heading: What If a Project Requires an Asbestos Survey?

Structures built before 1978 may contain asbestos and require a certified asbestos survey (AHERA) before demolition. We'll advise you on this requirement during your estimate. If asbestos is found, abatement must be completed by a licensed abatement contractor before demolition begins.

C&S Demolition works with certified abatement partners and can coordinate the full sequence.

sections.heading: How Much Does Chimney Removal Cost?
sections.body:
Chimney demolition in Southern California ranges from $1,500 for a single-story exterior chimney to $6,000 for a two-story chimney that passes through multiple floors. The price depends on height, construction (brick vs. stucco), whether the firebox is included, and whether the roof and ceilings need repair after removal.

Most chimney demo projects include the firebox, hearth, and full exterior stack down to the roofline or foundation.

sections.heading: Why Chimney Removal Is Complex
sections.body:
Chimneys are structural — many are tied into the foundation and pass through multiple floors and the roof. Demo requires careful sequencing so the structure doesn't shift, and the roof, attic, ceiling, and wall penetrations all need to be properly patched.

C&S Demolition handles the demo portion. We work alongside your GC or roofer to coordinate patching and waterproofing after the chimney is out.

sections.heading: Permits for Chimney Demolition in SoCal
sections.body:
Most chimney removals in Southern California require a building permit. The permit covers the structural impact of removing a load-bearing masonry element and the roof penetration repair. We handle permit applications in all 5 SoCal counties.

Lead paint testing is often required for pre-1978 chimneys — we'll advise if this applies to your project.

sections.heading: Get a Free Chimney Demo Estimate
sections.body: C&S Demolition serves all of Southern California for chimney and fireplace demolition. Call (562) 204-6335 for a free on-site estimate. We provide detailed quotes covering demo, debris removal, and any coordination needed with your GC.

excerpt: Selective demolition is precision teardown — removing exactly what needs to go without disturbing what stays. Here's how it works and when to use it.

sections.heading: What Is Selective Demolition?
sections.body:
Selective demolition is the precision removal of specific building elements — a wall, a ceiling, a set of cabinets, a section of flooring — while carefully preserving the surrounding structure. It's the opposite of a full gut job.

It's used in remodels, historical renovations, insurance repair projects, and any situation where you need surgical precision rather than full teardown.

sections.heading: Common Selective Demo Projects in SoCal
sections.body:
Removing a single wall to open up a floor plan. Removing a tiled shower and leaving the surrounding bathroom intact. Exposing plumbing or electrical in one section of a wall. Removing a dropped ceiling to expose original vaulted ceilings. Removing a specific floor section for sub-floor repair.

Each of these requires care and skill — damage to adjacent finishes or structures can be expensive to repair.

sections.heading: Selective Demo Cost in Southern California
sections.body:
Selective demolition is priced by scope rather than square footage. A single wall: $300–$1,200. A shower teardown (selective): $600–$1,500. Ceiling section removal: $500–$2,000. Full kitchen selective demo (cabinets and counters only, no flooring): $1,000–$2,500.

Call for a free on-site estimate — selective work is highly project-specific.

sections.heading: Why Hire a Licensed Contractor for Selective Demo?
sections.body: Unlicensed labor often causes collateral damage in selective demo — nicked pipes, cut electrical wires, damaged flooring adjacent to the work area. C&S Demolition's crews are trained for precision work and carry insurance that protects you if something goes wrong. Call (562) 204-6335.

sections.heading: When Do You Need Stucco or Drywall Removed?
sections.body:
Stucco and drywall removal is common in several situations: full remodel gut jobs, mold remediation (the affected drywall must come out), re-siding projects, window replacement (when stucco surrounds need opening), and water damage restoration.

In Southern California's older housing stock — lots of 1950s–1980s construction — stucco removal sometimes uncovers previous failed repairs or moisture intrusion that needs addressing before new work begins.

sections.heading: Stucco Removal Cost in SoCal
sections.body:
Exterior stucco removal: $2–$5 per sq ft depending on thickness and lath type. Interior drywall removal: $1–$3 per sq ft. Plaster removal (older homes): $2–$4 per sq ft. Full exterior stucco removal on a 1,500 sq ft home: $3,000–$7,500.

Pricing includes debris removal and haul-away.

sections.heading: Lead Paint and Asbestos in Stucco
sections.body:
Homes built before 1978 may have lead paint in the stucco or on the drywall. Homes built before 1980 may also have asbestos in textured ceilings (popcorn ceilings) or joint compound. California law requires testing and abatement before removing these materials.

We'll advise you on testing requirements during the estimate and can coordinate abatement when needed.
